entries.reason: the 6.1.3 armv7 cache's AVCaptureDeviceInput answers neither this selector nor any other of the multichannel-audio API (tools/corpus/objc-inventory.lua over ~/.charon/dyld/6.1.3/dyld_shared_cache_armv7), and the type of the argument, AVCaptureMultichannelAudioMode, is an 18.0 declaration SDK 16.4 does not make
entries.effect: YES for AVCaptureMultichannelAudioModeNone and NO for Stereo, first-order ambisonics and any number that is not one of the three, by the header's own reading of what the modes are (AVCaptureInput.h:357-362): None is 'no multichannel audio', which is what a single microphone records, and the other two are two and four microphones' worth of audio. The port's devices have one microphone (measured on an iPhone 4S and an iPad 2, facts/AVFoundation/AVCaptureDeviceDiscovery.md). Measured on this host, whose built-in microphone is a single one as well: 1, 0, 0 - so the port and the host agree on all three modes, and 0 for a number outside the enum

entries.reason: AVCaptureDevice is a class of 6.0 and neither -autoVideoFrameRateEnabled nor -setAutoVideoFrameRateEnabled: is an instance selector of any of the caches this port's bands are measured against (tools/corpus/objc-inventory.lua); the header declares the property getter=isAutoVideoFrameRateEnabled (AVCaptureDevice.h:404), so those are the two selectors an application compiled against a newer SDK sends, and the port defines exactly them
entries.effect: the value the last accepted -setAutoVideoFrameRateEnabled: was given, false until then - the header's own default: 'When you change the device's active format, this property resets to its default value of false' (AVCaptureDevice.h:399). Setting it goes through the header's refusal, below, so on this release no set is accepted and the getter answers false. The host's own camera answers 0 as well (measured), and its setter refuses for the same reason this one does

entries.reason: a CLASS property of a class of 6.0, and no release this port's bands are measured against carries the selector; the header declares it getter=isBackgroundReplacementEnabled (AVCaptureDevice.h:2521), so +isBackgroundReplacementEnabled is the selector a caller sends
entries.effect: NO, and the reason is that there is no choice to report: 'A class property indicating whether the user has enabled the Background Replacement feature for this application' (:2521). This release has no Background Replacement feature, no setting for it in Settings and no Control Center, so no user can have enabled it. The same shape as AVCaptureDevice.reactionEffectGesturesEnabled on a release with no Gestures setting (facts/AVFoundation/CaptureDeviceReactions.md). The host answers 0 here as well (measured: this Mac's own Control Center has Background Replacement switched off)

entries.reason: AVCaptureDevice is there and -displayVideoZoomFactorMultiplier is a selector of no release this port's bands are measured against; the member is macOS 14's and iOS 18's (AVCaptureDevice.h:1989)
entries.effect: 1.0. The header says what the number is for: 'In some system user interfaces ... the video zoom factor value is displayed in a way most appropriate for visual representation and might differ from the videoZoomFactor property value on the receiver by a fixed ratio' (:1987), and its own example of such an interface is the macOS Video Effects Menu. This release has no system interface that displays a video zoom factor, so there is no ratio to apply and the factor is displayed as itself. Measured on this host: 0.5, because that Mac's menu does display it, at half the capture value - so the two columns differ for a reason the header names
